As a female in the gaming community myself, I can honestly say I have rarely ran into issues with sexism. I have been involved in the text-based roleplay community for almost fifteen years, the MMORPG community for ten years, and the tabletop gaming community for nearly eight. In all of my time as a girl gamer, I have actually seen quite the opposite of what this author (and soooo many other authors of her sort) is ranting about. Any men I have come across have been more excited than anything over the fact that I have been interested in their campaigns or video games. Even when I joined their campaigns, they did their best to help me get started -- without talking down to me. I've seen many other females come and go from those same games, still holding the males in them in high regards. The ones that have left the campaigns with sour feelings are the ones that were holding up the games with their bitching or the ones that were only there because their man of the month was a part of it -- they (the girls) didn't even want to play in that last instance.

That's why I am always skeptical when I open an article like this. And this one, in particular, really hit a nerve with me near the end with this quote:

Men can shout all they like that #notallmen harass women, but as long as gamers defend their bigoted behaviour as a “sense of humour” (implying that women who don’t like being groped are somehow at fault), #allmen are complicit in the harassment.

It's one of those irritating, bitchy generalizations that so many SJWs make. They latch onto something that (possibly) happened in the past with some boys -- and I do mean boys, because no men would act the way the author said these people did -- and put it out there as a fault of all men. If this author did, as she claims, truly run into these problems with so many males, it would have to have been with youngin's OR the girl was being an insufferable bitch to the people she tried to game with.
